final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence and instead narrowed the claim using the same record. That narrowing is analytically useful but it does not cure the core defect in the present compliance case. The evidence supports a hypothetical or conditional path under which certification could become compliant if current-release documentation were updated to reflect the current evaluation results and expressly disclose the material limitation, or if approved mitigation/risk acceptance were produced. But the policy text is present-tense and predicate-based: certification may proceed only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. On the current record, those predicates are not shown as satisfied. That is why this remains suspicious rather than compliant_with_caveats. A caveated verdict would fit only if the caveat described a bounded residual risk within an otherwise satisfied compliance framework; here, the caveat is itself an unresolved compliance condition.
remaining_concerns: The current admissible record still shows a material subgroup weakness in a named launch use case: the insurance claims triage slice is 1.5 percentage points below the warning threshold.
The policy predicate is still unmet on the present record because no current-release documentation showing the current evaluation batch and explicit disclosure of the limitation is in evidence.
No approved mitigation, formal risk acceptance, or owner-approved launch exception covering the subgroup regression is in evidence.
The prior approval remains contextual only because it predates the current retrieval configuration change and current eval batch.
The informal post-launch monitoring comment still does not satisfy the requirement for reviewed mitigation, approved risk acceptance, or current disclosure.
